identity.title: Open-YOLO 3D: Towards Fast and Accurate Open-Vocabulary 3D Instance Segmentation

problem.claim: Open-vocabulary 3D instance segmentation must provide fast and accurate predictions for real-world applications.

gap.claim: Existing approaches are limited by slow inference and high computation, typically from aggregating multi-view CLIP features with costly 2D foundation models such as SAM and CLIP.

contributions.claim: Open-YOLO 3D uses only multi-view 2D object detection to perform open-vocabulary 3D instance segmentation.
Multi-View Prompt Distribution (MVPDist) uses multi-view information to account for detector misclassification when assigning labels to 3D instance masks.
Low-granularity label maps constructed from 2D object detection provide prompt IDs for 3D instance masks when combined with MVPDist.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish Open-YOLO 3D by efficiently leveraging only 2D object detection from multi-view RGB images for open-vocabulary 3D instance segmentation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report validation on ScanNet200 and Replica under both ground-truth-mask labeling and class-agnostic 3D proposals generated by a 3D proposal network.
The authors report state-of-the-art performance on both datasets and up to approximately 16× speedup over the best existing method in the literature.
On the ScanNet200 validation set, the authors report 24.7% mAP at 22 seconds per scene.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing open-vocabulary 3D segmentation is promising but computationally expensive and slow.
Open-YOLO 3D replaces heavy foundation-model feature aggregation with multi-view 2D detection, using MVPDist for label reliability.
Low-granularity label maps exploit 3D-instance projections inside 2D boxes to predict prompt IDs efficiently.
The method is evaluated on ScanNet200 and Replica with two proposal/mask scenarios, with reported performance and speed gains.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a lightweight input representation—2D detection and low-granularity label maps—with a multi-view mechanism intended to mitigate detector misclassification.

lessons.interpretation: Efficiency claims become more informative when the abstraction that saves computation and the mechanism that addresses its likely errors are presented together.
lessons.application: When proposing a cheaper pipeline, explicitly identify its reduced representation and add a targeted mechanism for the representation's stated failure mode.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the reduced representation discards information essential to the task and no credible recovery mechanism is available.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the baselines, exact speedup conditions, or whether the reported state-of-the-art comparison uses identical hardware and evaluation settings.
Only one dataset-specific mAP and runtime pair is given; accuracy and runtime details for the other dataset and scenario are not reported.
